name: Material Synthesis
premise: By 2035, backlash against purely digital AI art has driven a renaissance in physical making. Neural interfaces control advanced fabrication tools. World-model systems generate designs optimized for specific materials and processes. The art world fracture is about materiality: digital-native vs physical-first, ephemeral vs durable. Nia bridges both - uses AI to design pieces that can only exist physically, using materials in ways never attempted before.

neural_interfaces.capability: Specialized for motor control and spatial reasoning. Reads: motor cortex activity, spatial attention, hand-eye coordination patterns. Optimized for 3D manipulation and fabrication control. 32-channel EEG + EMG sensors on forearms.
neural_interfaces.mechanism: Direct control of robotic fabrication tools, CNC machines, 3D printers. Neural patterns translated to tool paths. Allows intuitive 3D sculpting at scale. System learns user's motor patterns and stylistic tendencies.
neural_interfaces.limitations: Requires physical proximity to fabrication equipment. Tiring - motor cortex activation is cognitively demanding. Limited to physical processes the tools can execute. Learning curve for each material/process combination.
neural_interfaces.social_impact: Brings prestige back to making. Artists are fabricators again. Combines traditional craft knowledge with AI optimization. Concerns about tool access - expensive fabrication labs create barriers to entry.

world_models.capability: Materials science and process optimization models. Understand: structural mechanics, material properties, fabrication constraints. Generate designs that are buildable and stable. Simulate aging, wear, environmental response.
world_models.mechanism: Physics-based simulation trained on materials data, engineering principles, fabrication outcomes. Proposes designs optimized for specific materials (ceramics, metals, composites, bio-materials). Generates tool paths for fabrication.
world_models.limitations: Conservative - tends toward safe, buildable designs. Limited creativity in material use. Doesn't understand artistic intent or emotional impact. Good at optimization, weak at exploration.
world_models.creative_role: Technical consultant and optimizer. Artist provides concept and aesthetic direction, system solves technical challenges. Like having expert engineer as collaborator. Enables previously impossible fabrications.

camps.digital_purists: Argue physical objects are anachronistic. Digital/virtual art is more democratic, distributable, environmentally responsible. Physical art serves wealth and private collection. See material focus as regressive.
camps.material_first: Counter that tangible objects have presence digital works lack. Physicality is essential to artistic experience. Digital art is ephemeral, lacks permanence. Making is essential to artistic practice, not just conception.
camps.hybrid: Blend digital design with physical realization. Use AI to push material possibilities. Argue the digital vs physical binary is false. Each medium has affordances worth exploring.

art_world_fracture.market_dynamics: Physical work commands premiums for uniqueness and presence. Digital work sells in editions, VR exhibitions, streaming rights. Hybrid work occupies middle ground. Collectors split between wanting objects to display and wanting accessible digital experiences.
art_world_fracture.what_matters: Provenance of physical objects. Authenticity verification. Material sourcing ethics (environmental impact, labor conditions). Craftsmanship and maker knowledge. Documentation of process. Durability and conservation.

economics.nia_position: Runs a 7-person studio: 2 ML engineers (materials/optimization), 3 fabrication specialists (ceramics, metals, composites), 1 structural engineer, 1 studio manager. Revenue ~$2.5M. High capital costs for fabrication equipment. Works with specialized material suppliers.
economics.commission_structure: Commissions $300K-$800K for large public installations. Material costs significant. Long production timelines (6-18 months). Pieces are unique objects. Some collectors commission smaller editions. Institutional commissions for public spaces.
economics.market_position: Nia is known for impossible fabrications - pieces that look like they shouldn't stand, materials used in unprecedented ways. Technical excellence combined with artistic vision. Work is collectible in traditional sense (physical objects with scarcity) but made with bleeding-edge AI.

surface.nia_work: Large-scale sculptures and installations combining materials in novel ways. Known for pieces that respond to environment (temperature, light, moisture) through material properties, not electronics. Explores form, balance, tension. Often site-specific.
surface.daily_process: Starts with physical material exploration - touching, testing. Works with AI to model possibilities. Neural interface sessions where she 'sculpts' designs in 3D, system refining for physical constraints. Fabrication cycles - iterative prototyping. Hands-on with materials throughout.
surface.studio_location: Industrial area with high ceilings, heavy equipment access, ventilation. Divided spaces: digital design lab with neural booth, fabrication workshop with robotic tools, material storage and prep areas, assembly/testing space.
surface.physical_artifacts: All work results in physical objects, often monumental. Materials: engineered ceramics, metal alloys, fiber composites, occasionally bio-materials (living elements). Pieces can weigh tons, require structural engineering. Permanent installations in public spaces, museums, private collections.

constraints.physical: Material costs and sourcing. Fabrication time. Physical limitations of materials and tools. Structural engineering requirements. Transportation and installation logistics. Storage space for large pieces.
constraints.social: High barrier to entry - requires expensive tools and space. Environmental concerns about material use and energy consumption. Safety regulations for large-scale fabrication. Need for specialized knowledge and team.
constraints.temporal: Long production cycles. Material curing/processing time. Shipping and installation windows. Permitting for public installations. Conservation planning for durability.
